title: animatedSprite3D
body:
## animatedSprite3D

Turns one named, forward-running Aseprite tag into a native editable AnimatedSprite3D with its own SpriteFrames, so a technical artist's authored per-frame timing survives into the Godot scene. Choose it when a sprite should play inside the 3D scene; choose sprite3D for a still picture. It reads the exported sheet PNG and its schemaxis.aseprite.sheet/1 metadata together, keeps every frame's rectangle and its duration in milliseconds, and plays the slice at an animation speed of 1 frame per second with each frame's duration written in seconds, so a 250 ms frame stays 250 ms. The scene plays the animation when it runs. Reverse and ping-pong tags, other tags in the sheet, trimmed frames and per-frame offsets are not imported; they are refused or ignored by design, never reinterpreted.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Godot stores frame durations as relative weights. Schemaxis fixes the animation speed at 1 frame per second and writes durationMS/1000, so editing the speed or speed_scale in Godot rescales every frame together rather than editing milliseconds.
- Only the tag named by animation is imported, and only if its direction is forward; reverse, pingPong and pingPongReverse tags are refused with UNSUPPORTED_ANIMATION_DIRECTION.
- Playback is qualified headless against Godot's own process frames at a fixed 1 ms tick. Godot carries a frame's leftover progress as a fraction across a boundary, so state can deviate from the ideal clock by up to about one tick times the duration ratio per boundary; this limit is exposed in the verification, not hidden. Rendered appearance and GUI playback were not qualified.
- Take file and metadata from the same Aseprite publication (sheet.png and sheet.json); a metadata width, height or rectangle that disagrees with the PNG is refused.

Native binding: `AnimatedSprite3D`. Output kind: `["image"]`.

| Input port | Multiplicity | Required | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `parent` | one node | no | `group` |

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `position` | Local position [x, y, z] in metres of the centre of the frame rectangle, relative to the parent group (or the scene root). Metres, Y up; the picture faces +Z and is not rotated or scaled by this node. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number","minimum":-100000,"maximum":100000},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3}` | `[0,0,0]` |
| `file` | The Aseprite sheet PNG: all frames in one non-interlaced 8-bit RGB or RGBA image of at most 4096 x 256 pixels and 524288 pixels, 1 MiB. Take it from an Aseprite operation's sheet publication with a workflow artifact reference (the third publication, zero-based index 2) or give an absolute path. The bytes are captured and hashed before Godot runs. | `{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":4096}` | **required** |
| `metadata` | The sheet.json published beside the PNG (schemaxis.aseprite.sheet/1): exact width and height, 1 to 32 frames with x, y, width, height and durationMS in whole milliseconds (1 to 5000), and tags. Use a workflow artifact reference to the fourth publication (zero-based index 3), the one published beside the PNG, or an absolute path. Unknown keys, wrong types, overlapping or out-of-sheet rectangles and a mismatch with the PNG are refused with the failing metadata location. | `{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":4096}` | **required** |
| `animation` | The name of the Aseprite tag to play. It becomes the SpriteFrames animation name, so it must start with a letter and use only letters, digits and underscores (at most 64). The tag must run forward; its frames are fromFrame to toFrame, counted from 1 and inclusive, and together last at most 8000 ms. Durations the fixed 1 ms playback check cannot tell apart (frames of only a few milliseconds, or a frame many times longer or shorter than its neighbour) are refused before Godot starts. | `{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":64}` | **required** |
| `loop` | true repeats the slice from its first frame after the last; false plays it once and holds the last frame. Omitted means true. This sets Godot's linear or no-loop animation mode; ping-pong is not offered. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `true` |
| `pixelSize` | World size of one image pixel in metres, 0.00001 to 10 (default 0.01). A frame 8 pixels wide at 0.05 is 0.4 m wide. Every frame of the animation shares it. | `{"type":"number","minimum":1e-05,"maximum":10}` | `0.01` |
